name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default. It skips past repetitive navigation straight to main content, solving keyboard users’ biggest pain point. Trade-off: it takes up a little space, but the clarity for screen-reader and keyboard users outweighs the visual cost.

name: Reader
text: A visible skip link risks pushing down primary content below the fold on small screens, making it harder for *all* users—not just keyboard users—to reach key information quickly. A hidden skip link with keyboard focus (like `position: absolute; left: -9999px;`) solves the problem without layout shifts, but only if we test with real screen-reader users to confirm they discover it. Settle it with a live usability test: measure time-to-task for keyboard users on both versions.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **hidden skip link** that only appears when focused via keyboard. It solves the keyboard user’s biggest pain point—repetitive navigation—without pushing down content for everyone else. Trade-off: screen-reader users won’t see it until they tab to it, but that’s the standard behavior they expect. This keeps the layout clean by default while fixing the core keyboard accessibility issue.

name: Reader
text: The hidden skip link still risks confusing first-time keyboard users who don’t know it exists—until they tab to it. A better alternative is a **small, high-contrast skip link that collapses into a visible icon on focus**, balancing discoverability with minimal layout impact. Settle it with user testing: measure time-to-task for keyboard users with both patterns.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a small, high-contrast skip link that collapses into a visible icon on keyboard focus. Result: skip link exists, visible only on focus, tested for keyboard/screen-reader users. Owner: accessibility-w1.
